The core log-filtering logic is correct (rules read in document order, `re.search` so a pattern like ERROR matches mid-line, tab-separated `name\tline` output with the newline stripped, break on first match, malformed XML → `config error: ...` + exit 2, unopenable log → `log error: ...` + exit 1, exit 0 otherwise). However there are two deviations from the spec:

The code instead writes `<rule name="error">: invalid regex`, wrapping the name inside an XML-like tag, so the emitted stderr text does not match the required format.

2. Unparsable XML file. The spec requires that when the XML file cannot be parsed the program prints `config error: <message>` and exits with status 2. The code only catches `ET.ParseError`, so a missing/unreadable XML file raises an uncaught `FileNotFoundError`, producing a traceback and exit status 1 instead of the required config error / exit 2.

Either of these prevents the code from satisfying the specified behavior.
